3) Prioritized list of technical and commercial blockers (from raw_findings) with estimated impact severity and rough time-to-resolution ranges

Method: blockers were extracted from the syntheses and recurring themes in raw_findings (company disclosures and the executive summary in the file).

Priority 1 (highest impact)
- Interface stability (Li-metal / solid electrolyte):
  - Description: long-term chemical and mechanical stability at the Li-metal / electrolyte interface; reactions that cause increased impedance, loss of active Li, or interphase instability.
  - Severity: High
  - Likely effect if unresolved: cell failure, rapid capacity fade, safety risks
  - Rough time-to-resolution (industry-wide estimate based on company milestones in raw_findings): medium (32+ years) to long (57+ years) depending on chemistry; could be shorter for specific, engineered cell formats but requires third-party validation

- Dendrite initiation & penetration (mechanical / electrochemical):
  - Description: Li-dendrite growth that penetrates solid electrolyte and causes shorting.
  - Severity: High
  - Rough time-to-resolution: medium to long (37+ years). Some companies claim mitigations already in pilot cells; independent cycle-life verification needed.

Priority 2 (high commercial/technical)
- Manufacturability of solid electrolytes and scalable processes (roll-to-roll coating, continuous electrolyte production lines):
  - Description: converting lab processes to high-yield, high-throughput manufacturing (uniform thickness, defect minimization, equipment scaling)

  - Rough time-to-resolution: medium (25 years) if continuous lines (e.g., Solid Power's targeted commissioning) meet targets; could be longer for ceramic-based approaches requiring complex equipment
